title: Inverted Index & Text Retrieval Pipeline
interviewAnswer: An inverted index maps terms to documents/postings containing them, making lexical search efficient. Real systems also tokenize, normalize, store term statistics and support field/position information.
why: Inverted Index & Text Retrieval Pipeline appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
deepDive: An inverted index maps terms to documents/postings containing them, making lexical search efficient. Real systems also tokenize, normalize, store term statistics and support field/position information. Positions enable phrase queries. Document/term statistics support ranking. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Index product descriptions so a query only scans postings for its terms rather than every document.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Inverted Index & Text Retrieval Pipeline make?
How would you validate or debug Inverted Index & Text Retrieval Pipeline in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
